verses.text: 1:1A certain man lived in the land of Ausitis whose name was Job. That man was true, blameless, righteous, and God-fearing, keeping away from every evil deed.
1:2He had seven sons and three daughters.

1:3His livestock numbered seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred grazing female donkeys. He had a very large body of servants and great enterprises in the land. That man was of noble standing among those from the sunrise.
1:4His sons would gather with one another and hold a drinking feast each day, taking their three sisters along to eat and drink with them.

1:5When the days of the drinking feast had ended, Job would send for them and purify them, rising in the morning and offering sacrifices for them according to their number, and one calf as a sin offering for their lives. For Job said, “Perhaps my sons have conceived evil thoughts toward God in their minds.” So Job did this continually.
1:6When that day came, behold, the angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came with them.
1:7The Lord said to the devil, “Where have you come from?” The devil answered the Lord, “I have come after going around the earth and walking through the world beneath heaven.”
1:8The Lord said to him, “Have you paid attention in your mind to My servant Job? For among those on earth there is no man like him—blameless, true, God-fearing, keeping away from every evil deed.”
1:9The devil answered before the Lord, “Does Job worship God for nothing?

1:10Hast Thou not fenced in what is outside him and what is inside his house, and everything around all that belongs to him? Thou hast blessed the works of his hands and made his livestock numerous in the land.
1:11But stretch out Thy hand and touch everything he has; surely he will curse Thee to Thy face.”
1:12Then the Lord said to the devil, “Behold, everything he has I give into your hand, but do not touch him.” And the devil went out from the Lord.
1:13When that day came, Job’s sons and his daughters were drinking wine in the house of their elder brother.
1:14Behold, a messenger came to Job and said to him, “The pairs of oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys were grazing beside them.
1:15The raiders came and carried them away, and killed the servants with swords. I alone was saved and came to report to you.”

1:16While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and likewise consumed the shepherds. I alone was saved and came to report to you.”

1:17While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “The horsemen formed three companies against us, surrounded the camels and carried them away, and killed the servants with swords. I alone was saved and came to report to you.”
1:18While this one was still speaking, another messenger came, saying to Job, “While your sons and daughters were eating and drinking with their elder brother,
1:19a great wind suddenly came from the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house. The house fell on your children, and they died. I alone was saved and came to report to you.”
1:20Then Job rose, tore his garments, and cut off the hair of his head. He fell to the ground, bowed in worship, and said:

1:21“I myself came out naked from my mother’s womb, and naked I shall depart there: the Lord gave, and the Lord took away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it happened: blessed be the name of the Lord.”
1:22In all these things that happened to him, Job did not sin at all before the Lord or attribute foolishness to God.
2:1When that day came, the angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came among them to stand before the Lord.
2:2The Lord said to the devil, “Where are you coming from?” Then the devil said before the Lord, “I have come after traveling through the world beneath heaven and walking through all of it.”

2:3The Lord said to the devil, “Have you then paid attention to My servant Job? For among those on earth there is no man like him—innocent, true, blameless, God-fearing, keeping away from every evil. He still holds to innocence, but you said to destroy his belongings for nothing.”
2:4The devil replied to the Lord, “Skin for skin! Whatever a person has, he will pay for his life.
2:5But indeed, stretch out Thy hand and touch his bones and his flesh; surely he will curse Thee to Thy face.”
2:6The Lord said to the devil, “Behold, I hand him over to you; only preserve his life.”
2:7The devil went out from the Lord and struck Job with a grievous ulcer from his feet to his head.
2:8He took a potsherd to scrape off the discharge, and sat on the dung heap outside the city.
2:9After much time had passed, his wife said to him, “How long will you persist, saying,
2:9a‘Behold, I will wait a little while longer, expecting the hope of my deliverance’?
2:9bFor behold, your memorial has vanished from the earth: sons and daughters, the pangs and pains of my womb, for whom I labored in vain with hardships.
2:9cYou yourself sit amid the decay of worms, spending the night in the open air,
2:9dwhile I am a wanderer and a hired servant, going from place to place and from house to house, waiting for the sun to set so that I may rest from the hardships and pains that now hold me fast.
2:9eBut say some word to the Lord and die.”

2:10He looked at her and said, “You have spoken like one of the foolish women. If we received good things from the Lord’s hand, shall we not bear the bad things?” In all these things that happened to him, Job did not sin at all with his lips before God.

2:11His three friends heard of all the bad things that had come upon him and came to him, each from his own country: Eliphaz king of the Temanites, Bildad ruler of the Shuhites, and Zophar king of the Minaeans. They came to him together to comfort him and visit him.
2:12When they saw him from far away, they did not recognize him. Crying out loudly, they wept, each tearing his own robe and sprinkling earth upon himself.
2:13They sat beside him seven days and seven nights, and none of them spoke, for they saw that his affliction was terrible and exceedingly great.
3:1After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day,
3:2saying:

3:3“May the day perish on which I was born,
and the night in which they said, ‘Behold, a male child!’

3:5May darkness and death’s shadow take possession of it;
may gloom come upon it.

3:6May that day and night be cursed;
may darkness carry it away.
May it not belong among the days of the year
or be numbered among the days of the months.

3:7But may that night be pain,
and may neither gladness nor joy come upon it.

3:8But may the one who curses that day curse it,
the one who is about to subdue the great sea creature.

3:10because it did not close the gates of my mother’s womb;
for it would have removed pain from my eyes.

3:11For why did I not die in the womb,
come out from the belly and immediately perish?

3:12Why did knees meet me?
Why did I suck breasts?

3:13Now I would have lain down and been quiet;
I would have slept and rested

3:14with kings, counselors of the earth,
who exulted in swords,

3:15or with rulers who had much gold,
who filled their houses with silver,

3:16or like a miscarriage coming out of a mother’s womb,
or like infants who never saw light.

3:17There the ungodly kindled the fury of anger;
there those worn out in body rested.

3:18Together the age-old ones
did not hear a tax collector’s voice.

3:19Small and great are there,
and the servant does not fear his master.

3:20For why has light been given to those in bitterness,
and life to souls in pain,

3:21who long for death and do not obtain it,
digging for it as for treasures,
3:22and become overjoyed if they obtain it?

3:23Death is rest for a man,
for God has shut him in.

3:24For sighing comes to me before my food,
and I weep, gripped by fear.

3:25For the fear I thought about came upon me,
and what I had feared met me.

3:26I had no peace, no quiet, no rest;
yet wrath came upon me.”
4:1Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

4:2“Have you not often been spoken to amid trouble?
Who will endure the force of your words?

4:3For if you admonished many
and encouraged a weak person’s hands,

4:4and raised up the weak with words
and put courage into powerless knees,
4:5yet now pain has come upon you and touched you, and you have become agitated.

4:6Is not your fear in foolishness,
and your hope and the innocence of your way as well?

4:7Remember, then: who perished while pure,
or when were true people utterly uprooted?

4:8As I have seen those who plow improper things,
those who sow them will reap pains for themselves.

4:9By the Lord’s command they will perish;
by the breath of His anger they will disappear.

4:10The lion’s strength, the lioness’s voice,
and the boasting of dragons were extinguished.

4:11The ant-lion perished for lack of food,
and lion cubs abandoned one another.

4:12But if some true word had been among your words,
none of these evils would have met you.
Will not my ear receive extraordinary things from Him?

4:13There were terrors and a nocturnal sound,
fear falling upon people;

4:14a shudder and trembling met me
and shook my bones greatly.

4:15A spirit came upon my face,
and my hair and flesh shuddered.

4:17‘What then? Can a mortal be pure before the Lord,
or a man blameless on account of his works?

4:18If He places no trust in His servants
and finds something crooked in His angels,

4:20From morning until evening they are no more;
because they cannot help themselves, they perished.

4:21For He blew upon them, and they withered;
they perished because they had no wisdom.’

5:1“Call, then, to see whether anyone will answer you,
or whether you will see any of the holy angels.

5:2For anger kills a fool,
and jealousy puts one who has gone astray to death.

5:3I have seen fools taking root,
but immediately their way of life was devoured.

5:4May their sons be far from deliverance;
may they be battered at the doors of weaker people, with no one to rescue them.

5:6For toil will certainly not come out of the earth,
nor will pain sprout from mountains;

5:7but a human being is born to toil,
and a vulture’s young fly to the heights.

5:8But indeed, I will entreat the Lord;
I will call upon the Lord, the Master of all,

5:9who does great and unsearchable things,
glorious and extraordinary things beyond numbering,

5:10who gives rain upon the earth
and sends water upon the world beneath heaven,

5:11who raises the lowly to a height
and rouses those who have perished,

5:12who changes the counsels of the unscrupulous,
and their hands will certainly do nothing true.

5:13He catches the wise in their understanding
and throws the counsel of the devious into confusion.

5:14By day darkness will meet them;
may they grope at noon as in the night.

5:15May they perish in war,
but may the powerless escape from a ruler’s hand.

5:16May the powerless have hope,
and may an unjust person’s mouth be stopped.

5:17Happy is the person whom the Lord reproved;
do not refuse the Almighty’s admonition.

5:18For He causes pain and restores again;
He struck, and His hands healed.

5:19Six times He will rescue you from distress;
and the seventh time no evil will touch you.

5:20In famine He will rescue you from death,
and in war He will release you from the hand of iron.

5:21He will hide you from the lash of the tongue,
and you will not fear coming evils.

5:22You will laugh at unjust and lawless people;
you will not fear wild beasts,
5:23for wild beasts will be at peace with you.

5:24Then you will know that your house will be at peace,
and the livelihood of your tent will not fail.

5:25You will know that your offspring are many,
and your children will be like all the vegetation of the field.

5:26You will come to the grave like ripe grain harvested at the proper time,
or like a heap on the threshing floor gathered in its season.
6:1Then Job replied:

6:2“If only someone would weigh my anger
and lift my pains together in a balance!

6:3It would indeed be heavier than the sand beside the sea;
but, it seems, my words are worthless.

6:5What then? Does a wild donkey cry out for nothing, rather than seeking food?
Would an ox raise its voice at a manger when it has food?

6:6Will bread be eaten without salt?
Is there any taste in empty words?

6:7For my soul cannot cease;
I see my food as a stench, like the smell of a lion.

6:8If only He would grant it and my request would come,
and the Lord would grant my hope!

6:9Let the Lord begin and wound me,
but let Him not destroy me completely.

6:10May my city be a grave, on whose walls I used to leap; I will certainly not hold back.
For I have not falsified the holy words of my God.

6:11For what is my strength, that I endure?
What time remains to me, that my soul holds out?

6:12Is my strength the strength of stones?
Is my flesh made of bronze?

6:13Had I not trusted in Him?
But help is far from me.

6:14Mercy has disowned me,
and the Lord’s care has overlooked me.

6:15Those nearest me paid no attention to me;
like a failing winter torrent or a wave they passed me by.

6:16Those who regarded me with awe have now fallen upon me,
like snow or ice frozen solid.
6:17Just as snow melts when heat comes and is no longer recognized as what it was,

6:18so I too was abandoned by everyone;
I perished and became homeless.

6:19Look at the roads of the Temanites,
the paths of the Sabeans, you who see clearly!

6:20Those who trust in cities and possessions
will incur shame.

6:21But you too have come upon me without mercy,
so that on seeing my wound you became afraid.

6:22What then? Did I ask you for anything,
or do I need the strength you have,

6:23to save me from enemies
or rescue me from the hand of rulers?

6:24Teach me, and I will be silent;
if I have gone astray in anything, tell me.

6:25But, it seems, a truthful person’s words are worthless,
for I am not asking you for strength.

6:26Your reproof will not stop me with words,
for I will not endure even the sound of a word from you.

6:27Except that you fall upon an orphan
and leap upon your friend.
6:28But now, looking into your faces, I will not lie.

6:29Sit down, then, and let there be no injustice;
once again associate with the righteous person.

6:30For there is no injustice on my tongue;
does not my throat ponder understanding?

7:1“Is not a human being’s life on earth a trial,
and his existence like that of a worker hired for the day?

7:2Or like a servant fearing his master and obtaining shade,
or like a hired worker waiting for his wages,

7:3so I too endured empty months,
and nights of pain have been given to me.

7:4If I lie down, I say, ‘When will it be day?’
And when I rise, again, ‘When will it be evening?’
I am filled with pains from evening until morning.

7:5My body is fouled with the decay of worms;
I dissolve clods of earth as I scrape off the discharge.

7:6My life is lighter than chatter
and has perished in empty hope.

7:7Remember, then, that my life is a breath,
and my eye will no longer return to see good.

7:8The eye of the one who sees me will no longer look upon me;
Thine eyes will be upon me, and I will be no more,

7:9like a cloud cleared away from heaven.
For if a person goes down to Hades, he will never come up again,

7:10nor will he ever return again to his own house,
nor will his place recognize him any longer.

7:12Am I a sea or a dragon,
that Thou didst post a guard over me?

7:13I said, ‘My bed will comfort me;
on my couch I will privately bring up a matter with myself,’

7:14Thou frightenest me with dreams
and overwhelmest me with visions.

7:15Thou wilt release my soul from my breath,
and my bones from death.

7:16For I will not live for ever, so as to keep enduring;
leave me alone, for my life is empty.

7:17For what is a human being, that Thou didst magnify him,
or that Thou givest Thy mind to him,

7:18or that Thou visitest him until morning
and judgest him for rest?

7:19How long wilt Thou not leave me alone,
nor let me go until I swallow my saliva in pain?

7:20If I sinned, what can I do to Thee,
Thou who understandest the human mind?
Why hast Thou made me Thine accuser,
and why am I a burden to Thee?

7:21Why hast Thou not brought about forgetfulness of my lawlessness
and cleansing of my sin?
But now I will depart into the earth;
at daybreak I am no more.”
8:1Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

8:2“How long will you speak these things?
The breath of your mouth is full of words.

8:3Will the Lord do wrong in judging,
or will the Maker of all disturb what is right?

8:4If your sons sinned before Him,
He sent them into the power of their lawlessness.
8:5But rise early to the Lord Almighty in supplication.

8:6If you are pure and true, He will hear your supplication
and restore to you a righteous way of life.

8:7Then your first things will be few,
but your last things beyond telling.

8:8For inquire of the former generation;
search out the family of the fathers.

8:9For we are of yesterday and do not know;
our life on earth is a shadow.

8:10Will these not teach you and tell you,
and bring words out of the heart?

8:11Does papyrus flourish without water,
or will a rush grow tall without a drink?

8:12While it is still on its root and unharvested,
does not every plant wither before it drinks?

8:13So, then, will be the latter end of all who forget the Lord;
for the hope of an ungodly person will perish.

8:14For his house will be uninhabited,
and his tent will turn into a spider’s web.

8:15If he props up his house, it will certainly not stand;
when he takes hold of it, it will certainly not endure.

8:16For he is moist beneath the sun,
and his shoot will come out of his decay.

8:17He lies upon a heap of stones
and will live among pebbles.

8:18If it swallows him up, the place will disown him.
Have you not seen such things?

8:19For such is the overthrow of an ungodly person,
and from the earth it will cause another to sprout.

8:20For the Lord will certainly not reject the innocent,
but He will accept no gift of an ungodly person.

8:21He will fill the mouth of true people with laughter,
and their lips with thanksgiving.

8:22Their enemies will be clothed with shame,
and an ungodly person’s dwelling will be no more.”
9:1Then Job replied:

9:2“Truly I know that it is so;
for how can a mortal be righteous before the Lord?
9:3For if he wishes to enter judgment with Him, He certainly will not listen to him, lest he answer back to one of His words out of a thousand.

9:4For He is wise in understanding, mighty and great.
Who grew hard against Him and endured?

9:5He wears the mountains out, and they do not know;
He overturns them in anger.

9:6He shakes the world beneath heaven from its foundations,
and its pillars sway.

9:7He speaks to the sun and it does not rise,
and He seals up the stars.

9:8He alone stretched out heaven
and walks on the sea as on ground.

9:9He makes the Pleiades, the Evening Star, and Arcturus,
and the storehouses of the south.

9:10He does great and unsearchable things,
glorious and extraordinary things beyond numbering.

9:11If He passes over me, I will not see;
if He passes by me, even then I do not perceive Him.

9:12If He takes away, who will turn Him back?
Who will say to Him, ‘What hast Thou done?’

9:13For He Himself has turned away anger;
beneath Him the sea creatures under heaven bent down.

9:14But if He listens to me,
He will surely sift my words.

9:15For even if I am righteous, He will not listen to me;
I will plead for His judgment.

9:16Even if I call and He answers,
I do not believe that He has heard me.

9:17Might He crush me with gloom?
He has multiplied my injuries without cause.

9:18For He does not let me breathe,
but has filled me with bitterness.

9:19For He prevails in strength.
Who, then, will resist His judgment?

9:20For even if I am righteous, my mouth will act impiously;
even if I am blameless, I will turn out crooked.

9:21For whether I acted impiously, I do not know in my soul;
I know only that my life is being taken away.

9:22Therefore I said,
‘Wrath destroys the great and the ruler,

9:23for the worthless meet an extraordinary death,
but the righteous are mocked,

9:25My life is swifter than a runner;
they fled and did not see.

9:26Is there a trace of a ship’s way,
or of an eagle flying in search of food?

9:27For even if I speak, I will forget while speaking;
bowing my face, I will groan.

9:28I shake in all my limbs,
for I know that Thou wilt not leave me innocent.

9:29Since I am ungodly,
why did I not die?

9:30For if I wash myself with snow
and purify myself with clean hands,

9:31Thou hast thoroughly dipped me in filth,
and my robe abhorred me.

9:32For Thou art not a human being like me, with whom I could contend,
so that we might come together for judgment.

9:33Would that our mediator were present,
one to reprove and hear the cause between us both!

9:34Let him remove the rod from me,
and let His terror not whirl me about,

9:35and I will certainly not fear, but will speak;
for I am not conscious of being so.

10:1“Weary in my soul and groaning, I will let my words loose upon Him;
I will speak, held fast by the bitterness of my soul,

10:2and say to the Lord, ‘Do not teach me to act impiously!
Why hast Thou judged me in this way?

10:3Is it good for Thee if I do wrong,
that I disown the works of Thy hands,
while Thou didst attend to the counsel of the ungodly?

10:4Dost Thou observe as a mortal sees,
or look as a human being looks?

10:5Is Thy life human,
or are Thy years those of a man,

10:6that Thou didst search out my lawlessness
and investigate my sins?

10:7For Thou knowest that I did not act impiously;
but who is there to rescue from Thy hands?

10:8Thy hands molded me and made me;
afterward Thou didst change and strike me.

10:9Remember that Thou didst mold me as clay,
and Thou art turning me back again into earth.

10:10Didst Thou not milk me out like milk
and curdle me just like cheese?

10:11Thou didst clothe me with skin and flesh
and thread me together with bones and sinews.

10:12Thou didst place life and mercy beside me,
and Thy care guarded my spirit.

10:13Thou holdest these things within Thyself;
I know that Thou canst do all things, and nothing is impossible for Thee.

10:14For if I sin, Thou guardest me,
and Thou hast not acquitted me of lawlessness.

10:15For if I am ungodly, alas for me!
If I am righteous, I cannot look up,
for I am full of dishonor.

10:16For I am hunted like a lion for slaughter;
changing again, Thou destroyest me terribly,

10:17renewing my examination against me.
Thou didst deal with me in great anger
and bring trials upon me.

10:18Why, then, didst Thou bring me out of the womb?
Why did I not die with no eye seeing me,

10:19and become as though I had not existed?
For why was I not taken from the womb to the tomb?

10:20Is not the time of my life short?
Let me rest a little

10:21before I go where I will not return,
to a dark and gloomy land,

10:22to a land of everlasting darkness,
where there is no brightness
and no seeing the life of mortals.’”
11:1Then Zophar the Minaean replied:

11:2“The one who says much will hear an answer in return.
Does an eloquent person also think himself righteous?
Blessed is the one born of woman who lives a short life.

11:3Do not speak at such length,
for there is no one to contend with you.

11:4For do not say, ‘I am pure in my works
and blameless before Him.’

11:5But how might the Lord speak to you?
He will open His lips to speak with you.

11:6Then He will tell you the power of wisdom,
for it will be twice what you have.
Then you will know that what has come to you from the Lord is worthy of the sins you committed.

11:7Will you find a trace of the Lord,
or have you reached the furthest things the Almighty made?

11:8Heaven is high—what will you do?
What do you know of things deeper than those in Hades,

11:9or longer than the measure of earth,
or than the breadth of the sea?

11:10If He overturns everything,
who will say to Him, ‘What hast Thou done?’

11:11For He knows the works of the lawless;
when He sees improper things, He will not overlook them.

11:12But a person vainly swims in words;
a mortal born of woman is like a donkey of the wilderness.

11:13For if you make your heart pure
and turn your hands upward toward Him,

11:14if anything lawless is in your hands, put it far from you,
and let injustice not lodge in your dwelling.

11:15For then your face will shine like pure water;
you will take off filth and will not fear.

11:16You will forget toil like a wave that has passed,
and you will not be terrified.

11:17Your prayer will be like the morning star,
and from noon life will rise for you.

11:18You will be confident, for you have hope;
out of anxiety and care, peace will appear to you.

11:19For you will be quiet, and no one will wage war against you;
many will change their ways and entreat you.
12:1Then Job replied:

12:2“So you are the people!
Surely wisdom will die with you!
12:3I too have a heart like yours.
12:4For a righteous and blameless man became an object of mockery.

12:5For at an appointed time he was prepared to fall beneath others,
and for his houses to be plundered by the lawless.

12:6But indeed, let no wicked person trust that he will be innocent,
nor those who provoke the Lord suppose that there will be no examination of them.

12:7But ask the four-footed animals, to see whether they will tell you,
and the birds of heaven, to see whether they will report to you.

12:8Speak fully to the earth, to see whether it will tell you;
and the fish of the sea will explain to you.

12:9Who among all these did not know
that the Lord’s hand made these things?

12:10Is not the life of all living things in His hand,
and the breath of every human being?

12:11For the ear discerns words,
and the throat tastes food.

12:12In much time is wisdom,
and in a long life knowledge.

12:13With Him are wisdom and power;
to Him belong counsel and understanding.

12:14If He throws down, who will build?
If He shuts people in, who will open?

12:15If He restrains water, He will dry the earth;
if He lets it loose, He destroys it by overturning it.

12:16With Him are might and strength;
to Him belong knowledge and understanding.

12:17He leads counselors away captive
and throws the earth’s judges into confusion.

12:18He seats kings on thrones
and bound their waists with a belt.

12:19He sends priests away captive
and overthrows the earth’s rulers.

12:20He changes the lips of the faithful
and knows the elders’ understanding.

12:21He pours dishonor upon rulers
and heals the lowly.

12:22He uncovers deep things from darkness
and brings death’s shadow into light.

12:23He leads nations astray and destroys them;
He lays nations low and guides them.

12:24He changes the hearts of the earth’s rulers
and leads them astray on a road they did not know.

12:25May they grope in darkness and not light;
may they wander like one who is drunk.

13:1“Behold, my eye has seen these things,
and my ear has heard them.

13:2I know as much as you know,
and I am not less intelligent than you.

13:3But indeed, I will speak to the Lord;
I will argue before Him, if He is willing.

13:4But you are unjust physicians
and healers of evils, all of you.

13:5May you be silent;
it will turn out to be wisdom for you.

13:6Hear the reproof of my mouth;
attend to the judgment of my lips.

13:7Are you not speaking before the Lord,
and uttering deceit before Him?

13:8Will you shrink back?
Become judges yourselves.

13:9Fine indeed, if He examines you!
For if, doing everything, you attach yourselves to Him,

13:10He will reprove you nonetheless.
Even if you secretly admire persons,

13:11will not His terrors whirl you about,
and fear from Him fall upon you?

13:12Your boasting will turn out like ashes,
and your body will be clay.

13:13Be silent, so that I may speak
and rest from anger,

13:14taking my flesh up in my teeth,
while I will put my life in my hand.

13:15If the Mighty One subdues me, as He has already begun,
I will surely speak and plead before Him.

13:16This will turn out to be deliverance for me,
for deceit will not enter before Him.

13:17Listen, listen to my words,
for I will declare while you hear.

13:18Behold, I am near my judgment;
I know that I will be shown righteous.

13:19For who is there to enter judgment with me?
For now I will be silent and fail.

13:20But grant me two things;
then I will not hide from Thy face:

13:21Keep Thy hand away from me,
and let Thy terror not overwhelm me.

13:22Then Thou wilt call, and I will answer Thee;
or Thou wilt speak, and I will give Thee a reply.

13:23How many are my sins and lawless deeds?
Teach me what they are.

13:24Why dost Thou hide from me
and regard me as opposed to Thee?

13:25Wilt Thou be wary of a leaf moved by wind,
or oppose me as grass carried by a breeze?

13:26For Thou didst record evils against me
and put the sins of youth around me.

13:28It grows old like a wineskin,
or like a moth-eaten garment.
14:1“For a mortal born of woman is short-lived and full of wrath.

14:2Like a flower that blossomed, he fell away;
he fled like a shadow and will not remain.
14:3Didst Thou not take account of this one also, and bring him into judgment before Thee?
14:4For who will be clean from filth? No one.

14:5Even if his life on earth is one day, his months are numbered with Thee;
Thou didst set a time, and he will certainly not go beyond it.
14:6Leave him alone so that he may be quiet and take pleasure in life like a hired worker.
14:7For a tree has hope: if it is cut down, it will blossom again, and its shoot will not fail.
14:8For even if its root grows old in earth and its trunk dies in rock,
14:9from the scent of water it will blossom and produce a harvest like a newly planted tree.

14:10But a man who has died is gone;
a mortal who has fallen is no more.
14:11For in time a sea diminishes, and a river, left desolate, dries up.

14:12But a person who lies down will certainly not rise until heaven is no longer stitched together;
they will not wake from their sleep.
14:13If only Thou hadst guarded me in Hades and hidden me until Thy wrath ceased, and set a time for me at which Thou wouldst remember me!
14:14For if a person dies, he will live, having completed the days of his life. I will wait until I come to be again.
14:15Then Thou wilt call, and I will answer Thee. Do not reject the works of Thy hands.
14:16Thou didst number my practices, and not one of my sins will pass Thee by.
14:17Thou didst seal my lawless deeds in a bag and mark whether I transgressed in anything unwillingly.
14:18And indeed, a falling mountain will fall apart, and a rock will grow worn away from its place.

14:19Waters wore stones smooth, and waters flooded the flat surface of the earth’s soil;
Thou didst destroy a person’s endurance.

14:20Thou didst thrust him away completely, and he departed;
Thou didst set Thy face against him and send him out.

14:21When his sons become many, he does not know;
if they become few, he does not understand.
14:22Only his flesh felt pain, and his soul mourned.”
15:1Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

15:2“Will a wise person give an answer from understanding of spirit
and fill himself with pain of the belly,

15:3arguing with words that ought not be spoken,
with speeches in which there is no benefit?

15:4Did you not also reject fear
and complete such words before the Lord?

15:5You are guilty through the words of your mouth,
and you did not discern the words of rulers.

15:6May your own mouth reprove you, not I;
your lips will testify against you.

15:7What then? Were you the first of human beings to come to be,
or were you formed before the hills?

15:8Have you heard the Lord’s command,
and has wisdom arrived at you?

15:9For what do you know that we do not know?
What do you understand that we do not also understand?

15:10Among us are both an elder and an ancient one,
weightier in days than your father.

15:11You have been scourged for few of the sins you committed;
you have spoken far too much.

15:12What did your heart dare,
or what did your eyes bring on,

15:13that you burst out in anger before the Lord
and brought such words out of your mouth?

15:14For what mortal can be blameless,
or one born of woman be righteous?

15:15If He puts no trust in holy ones,
and heaven is not pure before Him,

15:16let alone the loathsome and unclean man,
who drinks injustice as a drink.

15:17I will report to you—hear me;
what I have seen I will report to you,

15:18what wise people will say;
they did not conceal their fathers.

15:19To them alone the land was given,
and no foreigner came upon them.

15:20An ungodly person’s whole life is in anxiety,
and numbered years are given to a ruler.

15:21His fear is in his ears;
when he thinks he is already at peace, his overthrow will come.

15:22Let him not trust that he will turn back from darkness,
for he has already been assigned to the hands of iron,

15:23and he has been assigned as food for vultures.
He knows within himself that he remains destined to fall.
A dark day will whirl him about,

15:24and distress and affliction will hold him fast,
like a general falling in the front rank,

15:25because he raised his hands against the Lord
and stiffened his neck before the Lord Almighty,

15:26and ran against Him in insolence,
with the thick back of his shield,

15:27because he covered his face with his fat
and made a collar upon his thighs.

15:29He will certainly not become rich, nor will his belongings remain;
he will not cast a shadow upon the earth

15:30nor will he escape darkness.
May wind wither his shoot,
and may his flower fall away.

15:31Let him not trust that he will endure,
for empty things will result for him.

15:32His cutting will be destroyed before its time,
and his shoot will not grow dense.

15:33May he be harvested like an unripe grape before its time;
may he fall like an olive blossom.

15:34For death is the testimony of an ungodly person,
and fire will burn the houses of those who take bribes.
16:1Then Job replied:

16:2“I have heard many such things;
you are all comforters of evils.

16:3What then? Is there any order in words of wind?
What will trouble you, that you answer?

16:4I too will speak as you do, if your life were put in place of mine.
Then I will leap upon you with words
and shake my head against you.

16:5May there be strength in my mouth;
I will not spare the movement of my lips.

16:6For if I speak, I will not feel pain from the wound;
and if I remain silent, how will I be wounded any less?
16:7But now He has made me exhausted, foolish, and decayed,

16:8and Thou didst seize me; it became a testimony.
My falsehood rose up within me
and answered against my face.

16:11For the Lord handed me into an unjust person’s hands
and cast me upon the ungodly.

16:14They cast me down, fall upon fall;
in their strength they ran against me.

16:15I sewed sackcloth upon my hide,
and my strength was extinguished in earth.

16:16My belly is burned up from weeping,
and a shadow lies upon my eyelids.

16:17Yet there was nothing unjust in my hands,
and my prayer is pure.

16:18Earth, do not cover the blood of my flesh,
and let there be no place for my cry!

16:19Even now, behold, my witness is in the heavens,
and the one who knows with me is in the highest places.

16:20May my supplication reach the Lord,
and may my eye drip tears before Him.

16:21May there be a hearing for a man before the Lord,
and may a son of man plead for his neighbor.

16:22The numbered years have come,
and I will travel a way on which I will not return.

17:1“I perish, carried along by wind;
I need burial and do not obtain it.

17:2Weary, I plead—
and what have I done?

17:3Strangers stole my belongings.
Who is this one? Let him bind himself to my hand.

17:4For Thou didst hide their heart from understanding;
therefore Thou wilt certainly not exalt them.

17:5He will announce evils as a portion,
and my eyes wasted away over sons.

17:6Thou madest me a tale among nations,
and I became a laughingstock to them.

17:7For my eyes are hardened from anger,
and I have been greatly besieged by everyone.

17:8Astonishment seized true people at this;
may a righteous person rise against a lawbreaker.

17:9May a faithful person hold his own way,
and one clean of hands take up courage.

17:10But indeed, all of you, press on, and come now;
for I find nothing true among you.

17:11My days passed in a stench,
and the joints of my heart were torn apart.

17:12They made night into day;
light is near in the face of darkness.

17:13For if I wait, Hades is my house,
and in gloom my bedding is spread.

17:14I called upon death to be my father,
and decay to be my mother and sister.

17:15Where, then, is my hope any longer?
Will I see my good things?

17:16Will they go down with me to Hades,
or will we descend together upon a mound of earth?”
18:1Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

18:2“How long before you stop?
Hold back, so that we ourselves may speak.
18:3Why have we been silent before you like four-footed animals?

18:4Wrath has dealt with you.
What then? If you die, will the world beneath heaven be uninhabited,
or will mountains be overturned from their foundations?

18:5The light of the ungodly will be extinguished,
and their flame will not come forth.

18:6His light is darkness in his dwelling,
and the lamp above him will be extinguished.

18:7May the least people hunt down his belongings,
and may his counsel stumble.

18:8His foot has been thrown into a trap;
may he be entangled in a net.

18:9May traps come upon him;
the thirsty will be made strong against him.

18:10His cord is hidden in the earth,
and his capture upon the paths.

18:11May pains destroy him all around,
and may many come about his feet in severe famine.
18:12An extraordinary fall has been prepared for him.

18:13May the branches of his feet be devoured;
death will devour his beautiful things.

18:14May healing burst away from his dwelling,
and may distress hold him on a royal charge.

18:15It will lodge in his tent during his night;
his splendid things will be strewn with sulfur.

18:16Below, his roots will dry up;
above, his harvest will fall.

18:17May his memorial perish from the earth,
yet he has a name on the outer face of the land.
18:18May he thrust him from light into darkness.

18:19He will not be recognized among his people,
nor will his house be preserved beneath heaven,
but others will live in what was his.

18:20Those who came last groaned over him,
and astonishment seized those who came first.

18:21These are the houses of the unjust,
and this is the place of those who do not know the Lord.”
19:1Then Job replied:

19:2“How long will you weary my soul
and tear me down with words?

19:3Know only that the Lord made me like this.
You speak against me; without shame you press upon me.

19:4Yes, indeed, I truly went astray,
and error lodges with me—

19:4ato speak a word that ought not have been spoken;
my words wander and are not timely.

19:5But leave off magnifying yourselves against me
and leaping upon me with reproach.

19:6Know, then, that the Lord is the One who disturbed me
and raised His stronghold against me.

19:7Behold, I laugh in reproach and will not speak;
I will cry out, but judgment is nowhere.

19:8I have been walled in all around and cannot pass through;
He placed darkness before my face.

19:9He stripped glory from me
and took the crown from my head.

19:10He tore me apart all around, and I was gone;
He cut off my hope like a tree.

19:11He dealt with me terribly in anger
and regarded me like an enemy.

19:12His trials came together against me on my roads;
men lying in wait encircled me.

19:14Those nearest me did not acknowledge me,
and those who knew my name forgot me.

19:15Neighbors of the house and my maidservants—
I was a foreigner before them.

19:16I called my servant, but he did not answer;
my mouth made entreaty.

19:17I entreated my wife
and called with flattering words to the sons of my concubines.

19:18They disowned me for ever;
whenever I rise, they speak against me.

19:19Those who knew me abhorred me;
those I had loved rose against me.

19:20My flesh decayed within my skin,
and my bones are held in my teeth.

19:21Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, friends,
for the Lord’s hand is the one that touched me!

19:22Why do you pursue me just as the Lord does
and never become filled with my flesh?

19:23For who might grant that my words be written
and placed in a book for ever,

19:24with an iron stylus and lead,
or engraved in rocks?
19:25For I know that the one who is to release me upon earth is everlasting.

19:26May he raise my skin, which endures these things;
for these things were accomplished for me by the Lord,

19:28But if you also say, ‘What shall we say against him?’
and, ‘We will find a root of the matter in him,’
20:1Then Zophar the Minaean replied:

20:2“I did not expect you to answer back like this,
and you all do not understand more than I do.

20:3I will hear correction that puts me to shame,
and a spirit from understanding answers me.

20:4Did you not know these things from long ago,
since a human was placed upon the earth?

20:5For the delight of the ungodly is a terrible fall,
and the joy of the lawless is destruction,

20:6even if his gifts rise to heaven
and his sacrifice touches the clouds.

20:8Like a dream that has flown away, he will certainly not be found;
he flew off like a nighttime apparition.

20:9An eye glanced past him and will not do so again,
and his place will no longer perceive him.

20:10May lesser men destroy his sons,
and may his hands blaze with pains.

20:11His bones were filled with his youth,
and it will lie with him upon the mound.

20:12If evil becomes sweet in his mouth,
he will hide it under his tongue;

20:13he will not spare it and will not abandon it,
and he will hold it inside his throat.

20:14And he will certainly not be able to help himself;
an asp’s gall is in his belly.

20:15Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited up;
an angel will drag it from his house.

20:16May he suck the fury of dragons,
and may a serpent’s tongue destroy him.

20:17May he not see the milking of grazing herds,
nor pastures of honey and butter.

20:18He toiled for wealth in empty and futile things,
wealth he will not taste,
like gristly meat that cannot be chewed or swallowed.

20:19For he shattered the houses of many powerless people;
he seized a dwelling and did not establish it.

20:20There is no deliverance for his possessions;
in his desire he will not be saved.

20:21There is no remainder of his food;
therefore his good things will not flourish.

20:22When he thinks he is already filled,
he will be afflicted,
and every constraint will come upon him.

20:23If somehow he might fill his belly,
may He send a fury of wrath upon him
and shower pains upon him.

20:24He will certainly not be saved from the hand of iron;
may a bronze bow wound him.

20:27May heaven uncover his lawless deeds,
and may earth rise against him.

20:28May destruction drag his house utterly away;
may a day of wrath come upon him.

20:29This is an ungodly person’s portion from the Lord,
and the possession of his belongings from the Overseer.”
21:1Then Job replied:

21:2“Listen, listen to my words,
so that this consolation from you may not be mine.

21:3Lift me up, and I will speak;
then you will not laugh at me.

21:4For what then? Is my reproof from a human?
Or why should I not become angry?

21:5Look at me and be amazed,
placing a hand upon your cheek.

21:6For whenever I remember, I am agitated,
and pains grip my flesh.

21:7Why do the ungodly live
and grow old even in wealth?

21:8Their offspring are to their liking,
and their children are before their eyes.

21:9Their houses flourish, and fear is nowhere;
a scourge from the Lord is not upon them.

21:10Their cow did not calve prematurely;
their pregnant animal was preserved and did not miscarry.

21:11They remain like everlasting sheep,
and their children play,

21:12taking up a psaltery and lyre;
they delight in the sound of a song.

21:13They finished their life amid good things
and fell asleep in the rest of Hades.

21:14Yet he says to the Lord, ‘Go away from me!
I do not wish to know Thy ways.

21:15What is the Mighty One, that we should serve Him?
And what benefit is there in meeting Him?’

21:16For their good things were in their hands,
and He does not look upon the works of the ungodly.

21:18They will be like straw before the wind,
or like dust that a storm swept away.

21:19May his possessions fail his sons;
He will repay the man himself, and he will know.

21:20May his eyes see his own slaughter,
and may he not be delivered from the Lord.

21:21For what is his desire in his house after him?
The numbers of his months have been divided.

21:22Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge?
He Himself will judge murders.

21:23This one will die in the strength of his integrity,
entirely comfortable and prosperous;

21:24his inward parts are full of fat,
and his marrow spreads abundantly.

21:25But another dies in bitterness of soul,
never having eaten anything good.

21:26Together they sleep upon the earth,
and decay covered them.

21:27So I know you:
you press upon me with insolence.

21:28For you will say, ‘Where is the ruler’s house,
and where is the shelter of the ungodly’s dwellings?’

21:29Ask those passing along the road,
and do not reject their signs,

21:30for the wicked person is relieved for the day of destruction;
they will be led away for the day of his wrath.

21:31Who will declare his way to his face?
And what he himself did—who will repay him?

21:32He himself was carried to tombs
and kept vigil upon a coffin.

21:34How can you console me with empty things?
There is no relief for me from you.”
22:1Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
22:2“Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge?

22:3For what does it matter to the Lord
if you were blameless in your works?
Or what benefit is there if you make your way sincere?

22:4Will He reprove you out of consideration for you
and enter together with you into judgment?

22:5Is not your wickedness great,
and are not your sins countless?

22:6You took pledges from your brothers for nothing
and removed the clothing of the naked.

22:7You did not even give the thirsty water to drink,
but deprived the hungry of a morsel.

22:8You showed partiality to certain people
and settled them upon the land.

22:9You sent widows away empty
and mistreated orphans.

22:10Therefore traps encircled you,
and a terrible war threw you into turmoil;

22:11light became darkness for you,
and water covered you as you slept.

22:12Does not the One dwelling on high observe?
He humbled those carried away by insolence.

22:13And you said, ‘What has the Strong One known?
Will He judge down through the gloom?

22:14Clouds are His concealment, and He will not be seen;
He will pass around the circle of heaven.’

22:15Will you guard the age-old path
that unjust men trod,

22:16who were seized before their time?
Their foundations are a river flowing over,

22:17those who say, ‘What will the Lord do to us?
Or what will the Almighty bring upon us?’

22:18Yet He is the One who filled their houses with good things,
and the counsel of the ungodly is far from Him.

22:19The righteous saw and laughed,
and the blameless person sneered.

22:20‘Surely their substance was obliterated,
and fire will devour their remainder.’

22:21Become firm, then, if you endure;
then your fruit will be among good things.

22:22Receive an utterance from His mouth,
and take up His words in your heart.

22:23If you turn back and humble yourself before the Lord,
you have put injustice far from your dwelling.

22:24You will place it upon a mound, in a rock,
and, like a rock, the torrents of Ophir.

22:25Then the Almighty will be your helper against enemies,
and He will render you pure like silver refined by fire.

22:26Then you will speak freely before the Lord,
looking up cheerfully toward heaven.

22:27When you pray to Him, He will hear you,
and He will enable you to fulfill your vows.

22:28He will restore a dwelling of righteousness to you,
and brightness will be upon your ways.

22:29For He humbled him, and you will say, ‘He was arrogant’;
He will save the one with downcast eyes.

22:30He will rescue an innocent person;
and be saved through your clean hands.”
23:1Then Job replied:

23:2“Indeed, I know that the reproof is from my own hand,
and His hand has become heavy upon my groaning.

23:3Who, then, might know that I could find Him
and come to an end?

23:4I would state my own case
and fill my mouth with arguments.

23:5I would know the words He will say to me
and perceive what things He will report to me.

23:6Even if He comes against me with great strength,
He will not then deal with me by threat.

23:7For truth and reproof come from Him;
may He bring my case to its conclusion.

23:8For I will go toward the first things, and I am no more;
what do I know about the things at the end?

23:9When He acted on the left, I did not grasp it;
He will wrap around the right, and I will not see.

23:10For He already knows my way,
and He tested me like gold.

23:11I will go out in His commands;
for I guarded His ways and will certainly not turn aside

23:12from His commands; I will certainly not transgress,
and in my breast I hid His words.

23:13But if He Himself judged in this way,
who is there who contradicted Him?
For whatever He Himself wished, He also did.

23:15Therefore I am agitated about Him;
being admonished, I was concerned about Him.

23:15aFor this reason, may I be deeply troubled before His face;
I will consider and be terrified by Him.

23:16The Lord softened my heart,
and the Almighty agitated me.

23:17For I did not know that darkness would come upon me,
and gloom covered what lay before my face.
24:1“Why did the hours escape the Lord’s notice,

24:2while the ungodly crossed a boundary,
seizing a flock together with its shepherd?

24:3They led away the orphans’ pack animal
and took a widow’s cow as a pledge.

24:4They diverted powerless people from a righteous road;
together the meek of the earth hid.

24:6They harvested a field before its time, though it was not theirs;
the powerless worked the ungodly’s vineyards without pay or food.

24:7They made many lie down naked without garments
and took away the covering of their lives.

24:8They become wet from the mountain showers;
because they have no shelter, they clasped a rock.

24:9They snatched an orphan from the breast
and humbled one who had fallen.

24:10They unjustly made people lie down naked
and took the morsel from the hungry.

24:11They unjustly lay in ambush in narrow places
and did not know a righteous road.

24:14Knowing their works, He handed them over to darkness,
and at night he will be like a thief.

24:15The adulterer’s eye watched for darkness,
saying, ‘No eye will notice me,’
and he made a concealment for his face.

24:17For morning is a shadow of death to them all;
for he will recognize the disturbances of death’s shadow.

24:18He is light upon the surface of water;
may their portion upon the earth be cursed.

24:19May their plants appear dried up upon the earth,
for they snatched an armful from orphans.

24:20Then sin remembered him,
and he vanished like a mist of dew.
May what he did be repaid to him,
and may every unjust person be crushed like incurable wood.

24:21For he did no good to a barren woman
and had no mercy on a woman,

24:22and in anger he overthrew the powerless.
Therefore, when he rises, he will certainly have no confidence concerning his own life;

24:23when weakened, let him not hope to recover;
instead he will fall by disease.

24:25If it is not so, who is there who says I speak falsely
and will reduce my words to nothing?”
25:1Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:

25:2“For what prelude or fear comes from Him,
the One who makes the whole in the highest?

25:3For could anyone suppose that there is a reprieve for raiders?
Upon whom will an ambush from Him not come?

25:4For how will a mortal be righteous before the Lord?
Or who, being born of woman, could cleanse himself?

25:5If He gives the moon a command, it does not shine;
the stars are not pure before Him.

25:6Leave it, then: a human is decay,
and a son of humanity a worm.”
26:1Then Job replied:

26:2“To whom do you attach yourself, or whom are you about to help?
Is it not the One with great strength and a mighty arm?

26:3Whom have you advised? Is it not the One with all wisdom?
Or whom will you follow? Is it not the One with the greatest power?

26:4To whom did you announce words?
And whose is the breath that came out of you?

26:5Will giants be brought to birth
beneath water and its neighbors?

26:6Hades is naked before Him,
and destruction has no covering.

26:7He stretches the north over nothing
and hangs the earth upon nothing,

26:8binding water in His clouds,
and no cloud burst beneath it.

26:9He holds the face of a throne,
spreading His cloud over it.

26:10He circled a command upon the waters’ face,
until the completion of light with darkness.

26:11The pillars of heaven were spread out
and were astonished at His rebuke.

26:12By strength He calmed the sea,
and by knowledge He wounded the great sea creature.

26:13The bars of heaven have feared Him,
and by a command He killed the rebellious dragon.

26:14Behold, these are parts of His way,
and we will hear a mere drop of speech concerning Him.
But the strength of His thunder—who knows when He will act?”
27:1Job continued and said in his prelude:

27:2“As the Lord lives, who has judged me in this way,
and the Almighty, who embittered my soul,

27:3surely, while my breath is still within me
and divine spirit remains in my nostrils,

27:4my lips will not speak lawless things,
nor will my soul devise unjust things.

27:5May I never declare you righteous until I die;
for I will not give up my innocence.

27:6Holding to righteousness, I will certainly not let it go;
for I am not conscious of having done improper things.

27:7Nevertheless, may my enemies be like the overthrow of the ungodly,
and those rising against me like the destruction of the lawless.

38:25Who prepared a flow for violent rain
and a path for tumult,

38:26to rain upon land where there is no man,
a wilderness where no human exists,

38:27to fill untrodden and uninhabited ground
and make a growth of green plants sprout?

38:28Who is the father of rain,
and who gave birth to lumps of dew?

38:29From whose belly does ice come forth,
and who gave birth to frost in heaven,

38:30which descends like flowing water?
And who fixed the face of the abyss?

38:31Did you understand the bond of the Pleiades
and open Orion’s enclosure?

38:32Will you open mazourōth in its season,
and lead the Evening Star by its hair—lead them?

38:33Do you know heaven’s turnings,
or the things happening together beneath heaven?

38:34Will you call a cloud with your voice,
and will it obey you with a violent trembling of water?

38:35Will you send thunderbolts, and will they go?
Will they say to you, ‘What is it?’

38:36Who gave women wisdom in weaving
or knowledge of embroidery?

38:37Who counts clouds with wisdom
and inclined heaven toward earth?

38:38Dust has been poured like earth,
and I have fastened it like a cube to stone.

38:39Will you hunt food for lions
and fill the souls of dragons?

38:40For they have feared in their beds;
they sit in woods, lying in ambush.

38:41Who prepared food for a raven?
For its nestlings have cried to the Lord,
wandering and seeking food.”

39:1“Have you known the birth season of rock goat-deer,
and watched the deer’s labor pains?

39:2Did you count their months completed for birth,
and release their labor pains?

39:3Did you nourish their young beyond fear?
Will you send away their birth pains?

39:4They will break away with their young and multiply in offspring;
they will go out and certainly not return to them.

39:5Who is the one who let the wild donkey go free,
and who loosened its bonds?

39:6I made its dwelling the wilderness,
and its encampments the salt marsh,

39:7laughing at the city’s crowded bustle,
and not hearing a tax collector’s reproach;

39:8it will examine mountains for its pasture
and seek after every green thing.

39:9Will a one-horned beast be willing to serve you
or sleep at your feeding trough?

39:10Will you bind its yoke with straps,
or will it draw your furrows in a plain?

39:11Have you trusted it because its strength is great,
and will you entrust your works to it?

39:12Will you believe that it will return your seed to you
and bring in your threshing-floor grain?

39:13A wing of rejoicing creatures—neelasa—
if it takes hold of asida and nessa;

39:14for she will leave her eggs on earth
and warm them upon dust,

39:15and she forgot that a foot would scatter them
and wild beasts of the field trample them;

39:16she hardened toward her children as though not her own;
she toiled in vain without fear,

39:17for God kept wisdom silent for her
and did not give her a share in understanding.

39:18At the proper time she will lift up on high
and laugh at a horse and its rider.

39:19Did you clothe a horse with power
and put fear upon its neck?

39:20Did you put full armor upon it,
and clothe the glory of its breast with daring?

39:21Digging in the plain, it exults
and goes out into the plain with strength;

39:22meeting a missile, it laughs
and will certainly not turn away from iron.
39:23Bow and sword exult over it,

39:24and in wrath it will obliterate the earth;
it will certainly not believe until a trumpet signals.

39:25When the trumpet signals, it says, ‘Well done!’
From afar it smells war,
with leaping and shouting.

39:26Is it by your knowledge that a hawk stands,
spreading its wings, motionless,
looking toward the south?

39:27Does an eagle rise high at your command,
and does a vulture sit upon its nest and lodge
39:28upon a rocky projection and in a concealed place?

39:29Being there, it seeks food;
its eyes watch from afar.

39:30Its nestlings are stained with blood,
and wherever the dead are, they are immediately found.”
40:1The Lord God answered Job and said:

40:2“Will he evade judgment with the Mighty One?
Will the one reproving God answer it?”
40:3Then Job replied to the Lord:

40:4“Why am I still being judged,
being admonished and reproving the Lord,
hearing such things though I am nothing?
What answer can I give to these things?
I will place a hand over my mouth;

40:5I have spoken once,
but a second time I will add nothing.”
40:6Again the Lord replied to Job from the cloud:

40:7“No, but gird your waist like a man;
I will question you, and you must answer Me.

40:8Do not reject My judgment.
Do you think I have dealt with you for any other purpose
than that you may be shown righteous?

40:9Do you have an arm against the Lord,
or thunder with a voice like His?

40:10Take up height and power;
clothe yourself in glory and honor.

40:11Send out angels in wrath,
and humble every insolent person;

40:12extinguish the arrogant,
and make the ungodly decay immediately;

40:13hide them together outside in the earth,
and fill their faces with dishonor;

40:14then I will acknowledge
that your right hand is able to save.

40:15But look at beasts beside you;
it eats grass like oxen.

40:16Behold, its strength is upon the loin,
and its power upon the belly’s navel.

40:17It set its tail upright like a cypress,
and its sinews are woven together.

40:18Its ribs are bronze ribs,
and its spine is cast iron.

40:19This is the beginning of the Lord’s formation,
made to be played with by His angels.

40:20Coming upon a sheer mountain,
it brought joy to four-footed creatures in Tartarus.

40:21It sleeps beneath trees of every kind,
beside papyrus, reed and flowering rush.

40:22Great trees are shaded in it,
with shoots and branches of the chaste tree.

40:23If a flood comes, it will certainly not notice;
it is confident that Jordan will strike against its mouth.

40:24He will receive it in its eye;
catching in a snare, will he pierce a nose?

40:25Will you bring a dragon with a hook
and place a muzzle around its nose?

40:26Will you fasten a ring in its nostril
and pierce its lip with a band?

40:27Will it speak to you with a plea,
softly with supplication?

40:28Will it establish a covenant with you,
and will you take it as an everlasting slave?

40:29Will you play with it like a bird,
or tie it like a little bird for a child?

40:30Will nations feed upon it,
and will Phoenician clans divide it?

40:31All floating craft gathered together certainly cannot carry
one hide from its tail,
nor its head in fishermen’s boats.

40:32Will you lay a hand upon it,
remembering the war taking place within its body?
Let it happen no more.”

41:1“Have you not seen it,
nor marveled at what is said?

41:2Have you not feared because it has been prepared for Me?
For who is the one who stood against Me?

41:3Who will stand against Me and endure,
if the whole realm beneath heaven is Mine?

41:4I will not be silent because of it;
regarding a word of power, he will pity his equal.

41:5Who will uncover the face of its clothing,
and who could enter the fold of its breastplate?

41:6Who will open the gates of its face?
Fear surrounds its teeth.

41:7Its inward parts are bronze shields,
and its fastening is like emery stone.

41:8One sticks to another,
and breath will certainly not pass through it;

41:9each will cling to its brother;
they hold together and will certainly not be pulled apart.

41:10In its sneeze brightness shines,
and its eyes have the appearance of the dawn-bearer.

41:11Burning torches go out from its mouth,
and fire-hearths are hurled about.

41:12Smoke comes out of its nostrils,
as from a furnace burning with a coal fire.

41:13Its soul is coals,
and flame comes out of its mouth.

41:14Power lodges in its neck,
and destruction runs before it.

41:15The flesh of its body is joined together;
he pours down upon it; it will not be shaken.

41:16Its heart is fixed like stone
and stands like an unhammered anvil.

41:17When it turns, fear falls upon four-footed beasts
leaping upon the earth.

41:18If lances meet it, they will certainly accomplish nothing—
an uplifted spear and a breastplate.

41:19For it regards iron as straw
and bronze as decayed wood.

41:20A bronze bow will certainly not wound it;
it regards a stone-thrower as grass.

41:21Hammers were reckoned as stalks,
and it laughs at the shaking of a fire-bearing weapon.

41:22Its bedding is sharp spits,
and all the sea’s gold beneath it is like immeasurable mud.

41:23It boils the abyss like a bronze cauldron
and regards the sea like an ointment jar,

41:24and the Tartarus of the abyss like a captive;
it reckoned the abyss a place for walking.

41:25There is nothing upon earth like it,
made to be played with by My angels.

41:26It sees everything high,
and it is king of all things in the waters.”
42:1Then Job replied to the Lord:

42:2“I know that Thou canst do all things,
and nothing is impossible for Thee.

42:3For who is the one hiding counsel from Thee,
who withholds words and thinks he hides them from Thee?
Who will announce to me what I did not know,
great and wonderful things I did not understand?

42:4But hear me, Lord, so that I too may speak;
I will question Thee, and Thou, teach me.

42:5Before, I had heard of Thee with my ear,
but now my eye has seen Thee;

42:6therefore I despised myself and wasted away,
and I regard myself as earth and ashes.”
42:7After the Lord had spoken all these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “You and your two friends sinned, for you spoke nothing true before Me, as My servant Job did.

42:8Now take seven calves and seven rams and go to My servant Job, and he will make an offering on your behalf. My servant Job will pray for you, for I will surely accept his person. Were it not for him, I would have destroyed you; for you did not speak truth against My servant Job.”
42:9Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Minaean went and did as the Lord commanded them, and He released their sin through Job.
42:10The Lord increased Job. When he also prayed for his friends, He forgave their sin. The Lord gave double what Job had formerly, for a doubling.

42:11All his brothers and sisters heard everything that had happened to him and came to him, along with all who had known him from the beginning. They ate and drank with him and consoled him, and marveled at all the Lord had brought upon him. Each gave him one ewe lamb and an unstamped gold piece of four drachmas.
42:12The Lord blessed Job’s latter things more than the former. His livestock were fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen and one thousand grazing female donkeys.
42:13Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
42:14He called the first Hemera, the second Casia and the third Amalthea’s Horn.
42:15None were found beneath heaven better than Job’s daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
42:16After the affliction, Job lived one hundred seventy years; in all, he lived two hundred forty-eight years. Job saw his sons and his sons’ sons, a fourth generation.
42:17Job died elderly and full of days.
42:17aIt is written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord raises.
42:17bThis is translated from the Syriac book: he lived in the land of Ausitis, on the borders of Idumea and Arabia, and his former name was Jobab.
42:17cHe took an Arabian wife and fathered a son named Ennon. His father was Zare, a son of the sons of Esau, and his mother was Bosorra, so that he was fifth from Abraham.

42:17dThese are the kings who reigned in Edom, the land he himself also ruled: first Balak son of Beor, whose city was called Dennaba; after Balak, Jobab, called Job; after him, Asom, a ruler from the land of Teman; after him, Adad son of Barad, who cut down Midian in the plain of Moab, whose city was called Geththaim.
42:17eThe friends who came to him were Eliphaz, from the sons of Esau, king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minaeans.

This Bespoke reading edition follows the newer translation policy: ordinary address uses you/your, and direct address to God retains Thou/Thee/Thy. The existing Greek-based reading stream and separately dated comparison editions remain distinct.

The Greek additions, verse gaps, expanded speech of Job’s wife, and epilogue retain their existing labels. Difficult inherited renderings and transliterated terms remain provisional; familiar Hebrew- or Latin-based phrases have not been substituted for them.

INTRODUCTION

Introducing Job

Job is a poetic drama about a righteous man who loses his wealth, children and health, and wrestles with his friends and with God over why the innocent suffer. It ends with the Lord speaking from the whirlwind and restoring Job.

SETTING
Set in the land of Uz, outside Israel, it addresses all who face suffering and question God’s justice.
AUTHOR
The author is unknown; Jewish tradition attributed it to Moses. Modern scholars generally regard it as a work of wisdom literature by an unknown Israelite poet.
DATE
Set in the patriarchal age; composition widely dated between the 7th and 4th century BC.

Themes
Innocent suffering
The limits of human wisdom

Read in the light of Christ

The Fathers saw the suffering and vindicated Job as a figure of Christ, and Gregory the Great’s Moralia on Job read it in the light of Christ and the Church.
